title: Microsoft 365 admin center: rules that automate agent lifecycle management
summary: Hold: Microsoft now documents automation for two controls described as having no API. Tenant Configuration Management can apply agent user-access settings in preview, and the Package Management API documents rejection of pending publish submissions.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Lifecycle rules are reached in Microsoft 365 admin center at Agents > Settings > Agent management rules > Add rule.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to **Agents** > **Settings** > **Agent management rules**, and then select **Add rule**.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API for configuring the admin-center lifecycle rules.
claims.quote: Searched: '"agent management rules" "API" "Graph"' and Graph lifecycle rules utcm; read agent-settings, Package Management overview and utcm-agent-resources. Individual-package actions and three tenant settings are documented, not lifecycle-rule configuration.

claims.claim: Manual blocking and unblocking are at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block / Unblock.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **All agents**. ... select an agent from the list of agents. ... immediately under the agent's name, select **Block** or **Unblock**.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks an individual package.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Who may use agents is configured at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **Settings** > **User access** to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.claim: No API or automation is documented for the tenant agent User access control.
claims.quote: These resources also support remediation and applyOnce. ... userAssignmentCategory ... Specifies whether all users or no users can access agents and plugins. ... `everyone`, `noOne`
claims.fix: Replace this null API side and its rendered gap with graph 'POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors', docs https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta. Note: 'Preview; not supported for production applications. Set mode to applyOnce and include baseline.resources with resourceType microsoft.agent.useraccess, resourceVersion 1, and properties.valueObject.userAssignmentCategory set to everyone or noOne. This documents all/no users, not a specific-users selector. Requires delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All for the caller, delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite for the TCM service principal, and AI Administrator for the signed-in user.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-remediation-applyonce-resources.

claims.claim: Publish-request review is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > Requests > agent > Publish to store / Reject submission.
claims.quote: Select **Agents** > **All agents** > **Requests**. ... Select the requested agent ... **Publish to store** ... **Reject submission**

claims.claim: No API is documented for approving or rejecting agent publish submissions.
claims.quote: Reject a pending Copilot package title submission. This action reviews a package title and its submitted version; it doesn't reject an individual user's request. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{packageId}/reject
claims.fix: Replace this null API side and its rendered gap with graph 'POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{packageId}/reject', docs https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/package/copilotpackage-reject. Note: 'Beta, rejection only; production use unsupported. Requires Microsoft Agent 365 and CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All (delegated work/school or application). Use the confirmed pending title-review ID and supply the matching staged submission version in version; reviewerComment is optional. Rejects a title submission, not an individual user request.' Add the reference to sources. Do not equate this with automatic stale-request rule configuration.

claims.claim: A supported rule blocks ownerless agents without usage.
claims.quote: Admins can create a custom rule to block multiple ownerless agents that have no usage.

claims.claim: Applying a template to agents is a supported rule-based bulk action.
claims.quote: Use the **Apply template** action in an agent management rule to apply security policies to existing agents.

claims.claim: A supported rule rejects publish requests older than a specified number of days.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The Agent settings page does not list a separate automatic inactive-agent deletion rule.
claims.quote: Searched: '"agent management rules" "delete" "risky" site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-agent-365'; read agent-settings supported actions and agent-actions Delete agents. Settings lists five actions, none deleting inactive agents; manual soft deletion is documented separately.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: The Agent settings page does not specify a risky-agent rule condition or its signals.
claims.quote: Searched: '"agent management rules" "risky" "notification" delete scope' and agent management rules delete risky in microsoft-agent-365; read agent-settings, agent-365-overview and agent-registry-overview. No risky-agent condition is specified on Agent settings.

claims.claim: The Agent 365 management overview describes rules-based management blocking risky agents.
claims.quote: Leverage rules-based agent management to automatically enforce lifecycle policies, such as flagging ownerless agents, or blocking risky agents.

claims.claim: Eligible registry agents have a manual Install action.
claims.quote: **Install** | Deploys and installs the agent for the selected users at your organizations.

claims.claim: Manual Block and Unblock actions apply to a selected agent.
claims.quote: In the **All agents** page, select an agent from the list of agents. ... select **Block** or **Unblock**.

claims.claim: Installed agents can be manually uninstalled.
claims.quote: Admin can uninstall a previously installed agent.

claims.claim: The registry agent details provide a Pin for users action.
claims.quote: you can also select specific actions for the agent, such as **Install**, **Block**, **Uninstall**, and **Pin for users**.

claims.claim: Manual actions depend on agent platform and deployment state.
claims.quote: If you don't see the Uninstall option, the selected agent might not be installed. ... **Start and stop** ... This action is unique to Microsoft Foundry agents.

claims.claim: Pinning requires an agent deployed to some or all users.
claims.quote: You can only pin agents that are deployed to some or all users.

claims.claim: Blocking Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agents affects Copilot and other hosts such as Outlook and Teams.
claims.quote: Blocking or unblocking an agent that you created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio affects its availability and functionality in Microsoft Copilot. It also affects availability and functionality in other host products

claims.claim: Blocking SharePoint or Foundry agents affects only their availability in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Researcher and Analyst can be blocked tenant-wide but cannot be scoped through Edit users.
claims.quote: For the Researcher and Analyst agents, the **Edit users** panel is disabled. To manage their availability, block the agent for the entire tenant by using the **Block** action in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Agent settings also includes security templates.
claims.quote: **Security templates** - Create preset policies, rules, and allow lists for new AI agents to ensure consistency and compliance.

claims.claim: Agent and plugin access can be controlled by publisher category on the same settings page.
claims.quote: **Allow agents and plugins built by Microsoft** ... **Allow agents and plugins built by your organization** ... **Allow agents and plugins built by external publishers**

claims.claim: The same settings page includes sharing controls.
claims.quote: **Sharing** - Manage who can share AI agents within your organization and define the methods they can use to share them.

claims.claim: The same settings page includes tag management.
claims.quote: **Tags** - Manage the labels that admins and users apply to agents to organize and find them.

claims.claim: An agent can become ownerless when its original creator leaves the organization.
claims.quote: Agents become ownerless when their original creator leaves the organization.

claims.claim: Ownership reassignment gives the recipient owner rights over the agent.
claims.quote: The new owner gets full edit and delete permissions, plus access to any files the previous owner uploaded.

claims.claim: Deleting an agent in the Microsoft 365 admin center soft deletes it.
claims.quote: When you delete an agent in the Microsoft 365 admin center, the agent is soft deleted.

claims.claim: Soft-deleted agents have a 30-day recovery window.
claims.quote: You can restore an agent only while it's soft deleted and within its 30-day retention period.

claims.claim: Permanent agent deletion cannot be undone.
claims.quote: Permanently deleting an agent removes the agent and its associated resources and can't be undone.

claims.claim: The Agent settings page does not describe notification options for affected users or owners when these rules act.
claims.quote: Searched: '"agent management rules" "notifications" "Microsoft 365"'; read agent-settings in full and relevant agent-actions passages. Results describe SDK notifications or other lifecycle mechanisms, not user/owner notification options for these admin-center rules.

claims.claim: Viewing registry risk signals requires an E7 or A365 tenant licence.
claims.quote: Prerequisites for viewing risk signals ... Your tenant must have an E7 or A365 license.

claims.claim: Registry risk signals include contributions from Microsoft Purview, Entra and Defender.
claims.quote: Displays the Microsoft security platforms contributing risk signals for the agent, such as Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Entra, and Microsoft Defender.

claims.claim: The documentation does not specify whether these lifecycle rules consume registry risk signals.
claims.quote: Searched: agent management rules risky signals; read agent-settings, agent-365-overview and agent-registry-overview. Registry risk sources and general risky-agent blocking are described, but no mapping of those signals into an admin-center lifecycle rule is specified.

claims.claim: Inventory coverage includes Copilot Studio, SharePoint, Agent Builder, AI Foundry, Agents Toolkit, other Microsoft agent types and non-Microsoft platforms.
claims.quote: Specific platforms supported include: Microsoft Copilot Studio, SharePoint, Agent Builder, AI Foundry, Agents Toolkit, other Microsoft agentic types (such as Researcher), and non-Microsoft agentic platforms (such as Manus or Genspark).

claims.claim: Agent-management actions require administrators with the applicable management permissions.
claims.quote: The **AI Administrator** and **Global Administrator** roles have tenant-wide visibility and governance authority

claims.claim: The documented Graph block operation is beta.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Microsoft does not support using the beta block API in production applications.

claims.claim: The block API requires delegated CopilotPackages.ReadWrite.All.

claims.quote: Unblock (preview) | POST `/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/unblock` | Unblock a package to allow its usage.

claims.claim: The Package Management API can reassign an individual package's ownership.
claims.quote: Reassign (preview) | POST `/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/reassign` | Reassign ownership of a package to a different user.

claims.claim: Package Management mutation endpoints are documented as preview or beta.
claims.quote: Update package ... (preview) ... Block ... (preview) ... Unblock ... (preview) ... Reassign ... (preview) ... Publish ... (beta) ... Reject package title ... (preview)

claims.claim: Package block, unblock and reassign calls target individual packages rather than lifecycle-rule definitions.
claims.quote: POST `/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block` ... POST `/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/unblock` ... POST `/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/reassign`

claims.claim: Copilot Studio agent sharing limits are configured as a Managed Environments control in the Power Platform admin center.
claims.quote: You configure the sharing limits for agents as a Managed Environments control in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: These sharing limits apply only to agents requiring authentication.
claims.quote: Sharing limits only apply to agents that require authentication.

claims.claim: Sharing rules are enforced when users try to share.
claims.quote: Sharing rules are enforced when users try to share an app, flow, or agent.

claims.claim: Sharing-rule enforcement does not remove access users had before the rules were applied.
claims.quote: This enforcement doesn't affect users who already have access to the app, flow, or agent before you apply the rules.

claims.claim: Whether lifecycle rules can be scoped by environment, publisher or tag remains unspecified.
claims.quote: Searched: '"agent management rules" "conditions" "publisher" "tag"'; read agent-settings and matching Learn excerpts. Conditions and a subset of agents are documented, but no explicit environment, publisher or tag scoping options are specified.

claims.claim: All agents includes an Agents without owners card for reviewing ownerless agents.
claims.quote: When you select the **Agents without owners** card, the agent list is filtered to show the agents based on **Publisher type** and **Owner**. You can review the list of agents without owners and take appropriate actions for each agent
